title: Hosting Decision Framework & Throughput Benchmarks — Zenith Logix POC scoping
summary: Initial POC scoping to align on success criteria for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main goals: define workload sizing, target SLOs (p95 latency), cost ceilings, and benchmark plan. Security and data residency are gating items; customer leaning toward dedicated but needs evidence on cost/perf tradeoffs.
topics: Current stack and constraints (k8s on GCP, Vault/KMS, SSO)
Workload characterization: avg seq length, peak concurrency, typical prompt patterns
Benchmark metrics: p95 latency, tokens/s, throughput, token cost
Deployment modes: hosted API vs reserved Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem
Success criteria and go/no-go for pilot
Timeline and next steps for benchmarks and procurement
action_items: Maya Chen - Send controlled benchmark plan + template for load generator - due 2026-08-24
Diego Alvarez - Prepare suggested model variants (quantized and fp16) and expected token cost estimates - due 2026-08-26
Lena Ortiz - Share baseline infra limits and egress constraints, list of IP allowlists for Private VPC - due 2026-08-25
Arjun Patel - Confirm regulatory requirement for data residency for EU customers (yes/no) - due 2026-08-23
next_steps: Redwood to run 3-tier benchmark: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved, private VPC (if test infra provided)
Customer to provide sample prompt set (1000 prompts) and target concurrency numbers
Schedule 60-min deep technical benchmark run week of 2026-08-31
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 report link
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-21 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Zenith CTO), Lena Ortiz (Infra), Tom Reeves (Product), Guest Speaker 1

Summary (auto): quick alignment on POC success criteria and benchmarking plan, customer signals strong need for predictable throughput and data isolation.

00:00 Speaker 1: Okay, uh welcome everyone, thanks for joining.
00:06 Maya Chen: Hey thanks Arjun, appreciate you and team taking the time. We'll go through a short agenda: current stack, workload shape, success criteria, then benchmark plan.
00:18 Arjun Patel: Sounds good, um quick note we have limited bandwidth on infra ops in first two weeks of Sept so hoping to wrap pilot scoping this week.
00:28 Diego Alvarez: Got it. For context, can you run through your current inference pattern? token lengths, concurrency, any big spikes?
00:40 Tom Reeves: Yeah so most calls are customer-facing summarization and reranking. Average prompt is like 250 tokens, but we do have a lot of short prompts at 30-80 tokens. Peak concurrency is around 120 requests per second during our morning batch, sustained bursts of 30s to 2 minutes.
01:05 Lena Ortiz: And our infra is k8s on GCP, we're also using HashiCorp Vault for keys. We have strict egress policies and would need IP allowlist for Hosted option.
01:20 Maya Chen: Great, that helps. Our POC typically focuses on three axes: latency (p95 target), throughput, and cost per 1M tokens. For success criteria, what's non-negotiable?
01:36 Arjun Patel: We need p95 < 350ms for short prompts (<=80 tokens) and p95 < 800ms for longer ones ~250 tokens. Also cost needs to be under $X per 1M tokens — we didn't want to commit number in this call but let's say budget-conscious.
01:56 Diego Alvarez: Okay, reasonable. One nuance: hosted API will give fastest time-to-value and easiest benchmarking, Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency under high concurrency because you control GPU pools, Private VPC/on-prem trades some latency and increases ops but gives strongest data isolation.
02:19 Tom Reeves: Can you quantify the difference? Like how much latency premium for Private?
02:26 Diego Alvarez: It depends on hardware. If you run on same commodity A100s, latency mostly matches Dedicated. Where Private can add cost and network overhead is when it's on-prem or behind network hops; we see an added 30-80ms typical in some setups, sometimes more if there's poor NIC tuning. Also quantization (int8) can shave cost but might add slight quality delta, depends on your evals.
02:55 Speaker 1: and cache behavior? we have a lot of repeated prefixes...
03:00 Maya Chen: Good point. Redwood supports prefix/KV cache which helps repeated contexts. For Hosted we can enable managed KV caching. For Dedicated and Private you can configure local cache sizes; Diego will propose cache sizing based on your median context length.
03:20 Diego Alvarez: For benchmarking we'll measure warm vs cold requests, effective tokens/sec, and document token cost. We'll also capture model quality delta for quantized vs full precision on a small eval set you provide.
03:36 Lena Ortiz: Security concerns: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/HSM, data residency. Can you confirm SOC2 and do you provide access to audit logs for all requests?
03:51 Maya Chen: Yes we have SOC2 report; hosted customers get access to request-level logs in the console (with PII redaction options). Dedicated includes more granular audit logs and VPC peering for Private includes customer-managed KMS. We'll share security pack after call.
04:10 Arjun Patel: Procurement will want legal terms and possible add-on for dedicated reserved capacity pricing. Also curious about burst behaviour — if a spike overwhelms Dedicated, will you fallback to Hosted?
04:24 Diego Alvarez: We can configure fallback policies. Some customers use hybrid routing: reserved Dedicated as primary and Hosted as overflow for unpredictable peaks. We'll propose policies and cost math in the benchmark doc.
04:36 Tom Reeves: On model selection, we plan to try two model sizes: a latency-optimized 7B and a quality 13B. We want apples-to-apples throughput for those.
04:47 Diego Alvarez: We'll include quantized 7B int8, fp16 13B, and an intermediate 8-bit quant variant if you want to push cost lower. We'll provide expected token/sec and p95 targets for each.
05:02 Maya Chen: Timeline question: can we aim for a 2-week pilot? week 1 baseline hosted + small dedicated rack benchmark; week 2 deeper dedicated and private VPC run (if infra ready).
05:14 Arjun Patel: Two weeks is tight but okay if benchmarking runs are automated and we get clear templates. We really need go/no-go by 2026-09-09.
05:25 Maya Chen: Noted. We'll send a benchmark template today.
05:30 Speaker 1: Any immediate blockers for the private test?
05:33 Lena Ortiz: We'll need IP ranges and a support window to provision VPC peering. Also legal needs a DPA for on-prem test.
05:43 Maya Chen: Understood. We'll include a DPA draft and sample ipsec/VPC checklist.
05:49 Diego Alvarez: For success criteria recap, arjun, you said p95 < 350ms short, <800ms long, cost under customer threshold, and no unacceptable quality drop with quantization, plus SOC2 compliance. Anything else?
05:58 Arjun Patel: Also throughput: sustain 6k tokens/sec during peak without p95 spike above targets.
06:08 Tom Reeves: And we want a scoring rubric for quality: rouge/semantic score on 200 examples.
06:15 Maya Chen: We'll include that in the eval plan.
06:20 Speaker 1: Okay last bit — procurement wants comparison matrix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with cost, ops burden, time-to-prod, security posture.
06:29 Maya Chen: We'll attach a one-pager.
06:32 Diego Alvarez: I'll lay out the benchmarking steps: 1) ingest sample prompts, 2) run baseline hosted 2-hour run with synthetic concurrency matching your morning spikes, 3) spin reserved Dedicated 1-rack test with same load, 4) if private infra ready, run with VPC peering.
06:55 Lena Ortiz: For the private run, we may need to schedule maintenance windows. We'll propose two dates next week.
07:05 Maya Chen: Great. Recap of next steps: Redwood sends benchmark plan + security pack + DPA; customer provides prompts, concurrency, and infra details; schedule deep benchmark run during week of 2026-08-31.
07:20 Arjun Patel: That works. Thanks everyone.
07:24 Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with action items in email.
07:30 [call ends]

Notes: Transcription contains occasional speaker mislabels and minor word errors (e.g., K V cache instead of KV cache).
